item.title: The Daily Plant — Sumac (Rhus)
item.description:
A deep dive on the native sumacs — Rhus typhina, glabra, copallinum, and aromatica — right as their fruit panicles turn crimson and fall color starts to build. item.title: The Daily Plant — Bluestem Grasses (Andropogon and Anatherum)
item.description:
A deep dive on the bluestem complex at the height of its late-summer bloom: Andropogon gerardii and Andropogon ternarius, the true bluestems, alongside their recently reclassified relatives Anatherum glomeratum and Anatherum virginicum, formerly lumped together as Andropogon. item.title: The Daily Plant — Franklin Tree (Franklinia alatamaha)
item.description:
A deep dive on Franklinia alatamaha, the Georgia native that has been extinct in the wild for two centuries and survives only as cultivated descendants of William Bartram's original seed collection. We cover the extinction mystery, the narrow cultural window that makes it a specimen rather than a workhorse, its late-summer-into-fall bloom that fills a real calendar gap, and how to weigh it against Stewartia pseudocamellia and Gordonia lasianthus in a design. Closes with a recall quiz on Pycnanthemum, Microstegium vimineum, and Chelone.

item.description:

item.title: The Daily Plant — Native Sunflowers (Helianthus)
item.description:
An expert-level genus deep dive on Helianthus, the native perennial sunflowers of the East Coast.
